questions.prompt: You asked one question. /usage shows a cost far larger than the question's length explains. What accounts for most of it?
options: The question was re-tokenized once per candidate answer the model considered
One turn can drive several requests, and each re-sends the whole prompt — history, files, and tool definitions included
The API bills the request once for the prompt and again for the model's internal draft
The prompt cache was cold, so the entire input was charged at full price three times
questions.explanation: A single user turn is usually several round trips — read a file, run a command, check a result — and every one of those re-sends the full assembled prompt. That is why cost tracks context, not question length. Option C invents a double-billing model that does not exist. Option D is wrong because the cache reads at a reduced rate, and 'three times' is not what the re-send loop does.

questions.prompt: The agent ignores a clear instruction you gave and follows a rule from the project's CLAUDE.md instead. Which is the accurate diagnosis?
options: Your instruction lost to the system prompt, which always outranks everything
The context window dropped your message during compaction
Project files are injected into the context on every request and were present alongside your words
The model cannot see your instruction unless it is inside a code block
questions.explanation: Your message and the project file arrived in the same context, so the agent reconciled them and went with the one that read as a standing project rule. Option A gets the mechanism backwards — your message is not competing against a system prompt, it is competing against a file the harness loaded. Option B needs a window fill, and this happened on a fresh session. Option D is not how input works.

questions.prompt: You are extracting issue titles into JSON and two runs of the identical request produce slightly different arrays. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Add more examples of the output you want
Tighten the format instruction so only the array is produced, and lower the temperature if you control it
Ask the agent to check its work before answering
Clear the context before each run so the window is identical
questions.explanation: Variation in a formatted extraction is sampling, so the fix is the one that removes sampling freedom: a tight output contract plus a lower temperature. Option A adds input without removing freedom. Option C asks for reasoning where the problem is the sampler, and verification cannot fix a non-deterministic draw. Option D is a real hygiene move but the window was already identical within a single turn — the run-to-run difference is the model, not the context.
